root_cause.text: ieee80211_tx_prepare_skb() in mac80211 had inconsistent skb ownership on failure because its TX_DROP error path returned false without freeing the sk_buff, unlike its other failure paths, causing callers to leak the skb or handle ownership inconsistently.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states “ieee80211_tx_prepare_skb() has three error paths, but only two of them free the skb. The first error path (ieee80211_tx_prepare() returning TX_DROP) does not free it,” and the patch adds `kfree_skb(skb);` before `return false;` in `net/mac80211/tx.c` while removing caller-side frees in ath9k, mt76, and mac80211_hwsim and documenting that “On failure, the skb is freed by this function.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Return immediately when probe skb preparation fails instead of using the generic error path.
intent_record.what: In ath_scan_send_probe(), the failure path after ieee80211_tx_prepare_skb(sc->hw, vif, skb, band, NULL) was changed from `goto error;` to `return;` when preparation returns false.
intent_record.how: At runtime, if skb transmission preparation fails, the function now exits immediately instead of jumping to the shared error label, changing the cleanup/error-path behavior for that specific failure case and avoiding execution of the code associated with the `error` label.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop freeing the skb on ieee80211_tx_prepare_skb() failure and just return false to avoid incorrect skb ownership handling.
intent_record.what: The change removes the braces and the call to dev_kfree_skb_any(skb) from the failure path of the if (!ieee80211_tx_prepare_skb(sc->hw, vif, skb, band, &sta)) check, leaving only an immediate return false when skb preparation fails.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when ieee80211_tx_prepare_skb() fails, the function now returns false without explicitly freeing the skb in this branch. This avoids freeing the buffer here, likely relying on the callee or another caller-side path to manage skb ownership and preventing an incorrect or duplicate free.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid freeing the probe skb on ieee80211_tx_prepare_skb() failure because cleanup is handled by the common exit path or lower layer.
intent_record.what: The change removes the call to ieee80211_free_txskb(phy->hw, skb) from the failure path of the if (!ieee80211_tx_prepare_skb(...)) check, leaving only a goto out when skb preparation fails.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when ieee80211_tx_prepare_skb() returns false, the function no longer explicitly frees the skb before jumping to the out label, preventing this path from releasing the buffer at that point and avoiding an incorrect or duplicate free if cleanup is handled elsewhere.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove an incorrect skb free in hw_scan_work() to avoid premature or duplicate release of the probe buffer on a scan failure path.
intent_record.what: The call to kfree_skb(probe); was removed from the conditional path that executes after rcu_read_unlock() and before continue when the preceding check fails inside hw_scan_work().
intent_record.how: At runtime, this stops the probe skb from being freed in that specific failure path, avoiding disposal of the buffer there and leaving its lifetime to be handled elsewhere instead of potentially freeing it prematurely or twice.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clarify the helper's documentation to state that it frees the skb on failure so callers do not free it twice.
intent_record.what: The function comment for the skb preparation helper was updated to add a period to the return description and to document that when preparation fails, the function frees the skb and callers must not free it again.
intent_record.how: This does not change runtime behavior, but it clarifies ownership and failure semantics so callers understand that the skb is already released on failure, helping prevent double-free misuse.

intent_record.intent_summary: Free the skb when transmission preparation drops the packet to avoid a memory leak in ieee80211_tx_prepare_skb().
intent_record.what: The change wraps the existing TX_DROP check in braces and adds a call to kfree_skb(skb) before returning false from ieee80211_tx_prepare_skb().
intent_record.how: When ieee80211_tx_prepare() indicates the packet should be dropped, the skb is now explicitly freed before the function exits, preventing the dropped buffer from remaining allocated and leaking memory.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 06be6b149f7e406bcf16098567f5a6c9f042bced
Author: Felix Fietkau <nbd@openwrt.org>
Date:   Mon Oct 14 18:01:00 2013 +0200

    mac80211: add ieee80211_tx_prepare_skb() helper function
    
    This can be used by a driver to prepare skbs for transmission, which were
    obtained via functions such as ieee80211_probereq_get or
    ieee80211_nullfunc_get.
    
    This is useful for drivers that want to send those frames directly, but
    need rate control information to be prepared first.
bic_trace_step.reason: The function body is sufficient to determine the ownership/error-path behavior. The vulnerable construct is present: on the first failure path, `if (ieee80211_tx_prepare(sdata, &tx, skb) == TX_DROP) return false;` returns `false` directly without freeing `skb`. Per the stated root cause, the TX_DROP path in `ieee80211_tx_prepare_skb()` should not leave skb ownership inconsistent. The function also has another failure path, `if (invoke_tx_handlers(&tx)) return false;`, but there is no visible cleanup in either return site. Since the root cause specifically identifies the `TX_DROP` error path returning false without freeing the sk_buff, that exact vulnerable logic is present here. No fix is shown in this function, such as freeing the skb on the TX_DROP path or otherwise making ownership consistent before returning false.

commit 97b045d62bffae5a91a286b56ac51db0c4385687
Author: Johannes Berg <johannes@sipsolutions.net>
Date:   Fri Jun 20 01:22:30 2008 +0200

    mac80211: add single function calling tx handlers
    
    This modifies mac80211 to only have a single function calling the
    TX handlers rather than them being invoked in multiple places.
    
    Signed-off-by: Johannes Berg <johannes@sipsolutions.net>
    Signed-off-by: John W. Linville <linville@tuxdriver.com>

diff --git a/net/mac80211/tx.c b/net/m
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the relevant TX handler failure-path ownership logic clearly, so it is sufficient. The new helper `invoke_tx_handlers()` explicitly handles `TX_DROP` by freeing the skb: `if (unlikely(res == TX_DROP)) { ... dev_kfree_skb(skb); ... return -1; }`. This is exactly the missing ownership handling described in the root cause. It also frees any `extra_frag[]` buffers and `tx->extra_frag`, making the drop path self-contained. Callers then treat any non-zero return as terminal (`if (invoke_tx_handlers(&tx)) goto out;` in `ieee80211_tx()`, and `if (invoke_tx_handlers(&tx)) skb = NULL;` in `ieee80211_get_buffered_bc()`), without needing to free the skb themselves on `TX_DROP`. Therefore the vulnerable construct—returning failure on `TX_DROP` without freeing the skb—is absent here, and the fix is already present.
